title: Template Method and State
idea: Template Method fixes the order of an algorithm's steps in a base class and lets subclasses fill them in; State gives each mode its own object.

analogy.text: A coffee machine. Every drink runs grind, brew, pour; only the brew step differs per drink. The start button's effect depends on mode: idle, brewing, or empty.
analogy.breaks: A real machine is one box; code gives each state its own class.

points: A template method calls step methods in a fixed order; subclasses override steps.
A hook is a step with a default body that subclasses may override.
In State, the context forwards every call to its current state object.
Each state decides which state comes next, so no central `switch` exists.

edges.label: submit
edges.caption: `Draft.submit` swaps the document's state object for an `InReview`. The document class itself has no branch.

edges.label: reject
edges.caption: `InReview.reject` sends it back. Each state knows only its own legal moves.

edges.label: approve
edges.caption: `InReview.approve` moves to `Published`, which refuses every later action.

code.title: Template Method
code.caption: Add a `MarkdownReport` that overrides only `header` and `row`, and render the same rows.

walk.text: `render` is the template method: header, rows, footer, always in this order.
Required steps throw in the base class, so a missing override fails loudly.
`footer` is a hook: it has a default, and overriding it is optional.
`CsvReport` fills the two required steps and keeps the default footer.
`TextReport` also overrides the hook. Neither subclass touches `render`.

code.title: State
code.caption: Add an `archive` action that only `Published` accepts. Notice which classes you must edit.

walk.text: `Draft` accepts `submit` and moves the document on. Other actions are refused.
`InReview` can approve or send the document back to `Draft`.
`Published` is final: every action is refused.
The context holds one state object; `moveTo` replaces it.
Each action forwards to the current state, then reports the new status.
One document receives six actions; the output shows each refusal and move.

pitfalls: Never let subclasses override the template method itself; that breaks the fixed order.
Deep Template Method trees turn rigid; pass steps in as objects when variations multiply.
Use State only when behaviour truly differs per mode; a status field may suffice.

options: TypeError: this.add is not a function
quiz.why: `make` is the template. `add` comes from `Tea` and `pour` from `Iced`; each step resolves on the instance's prototype chain.

takeaway: Template Method varies steps by subclass; State varies behaviour as modes change.
